section_summary: This section contains intelligence reports, diplomatic despatches, memoranda, letters, telegrams, and cross-reference sheets concerning Japan's chemical and related manufacturing industries between 1940 and 1943. Key subjects include Japanese production and capacities in caustic soda, soda ash, synthetic nitrogen, ammonium sulphate, cyanamide, dyestuffs, pyrites, and agricultural fertilisers, alongside evaluations of critical resource vulnerabilities such as industrial salt, potash, and carbon black. The documents also reflect Anglo-American economic intelligence coordination through the British Ministry of Economic Warfare, Chilean iodine negotiations, and reports on wartime corporate conversions to aviation and metallurgical production.

subfiles.about: A naval intelligence report on the development, production statistics, manufacturing processes, key producers, and raw material vulnerabilities of the Japanese soda industry.
subfiles.from: H. H. Smith-Hutton, Lieutenant Commander, U.S. Navy, Naval Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Surveys Japan's rapidly expanding soda industry, detailing caustic soda and soda ash output, major manufacturing companies, and vulnerability to industrial salt import disruptions.
subfiles.title: Intelligence Report No. 147: Soda Industry
subfiles.to: Chief of Naval Operations, Navy Department

subfiles.about: A record of conversation between Secretary of State Hull and Chilean Ambassador Michels regarding Japanese efforts to purchase Chilean crude iodine stored in Japan using frozen funds.
subfiles.summary: Secretary Hull and Chilean Ambassador Michels discussed Japan's offer to buy Chilean crude iodine in Japan using frozen funds, and the broader threat of Axis aggression in the Western Hemisphere.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Desire of Japan to Purchase Iodine Held by Chilean Corporation

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet referencing a telegram regarding specialized machines and automotive parts formerly shipped to Japan by European manufacturers.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a telegram regarding European shipments of specialized machinery and automotive parts to Japan.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Automotive Parts and Specialized Machines for Japan

subfiles.about: A formal request from the Chemical Warfare Service to the Department of State for twenty-six specific consular reports on the Japanese chemical industry.
subfiles.from: Sidney L. Weedon, Major, Chemical Warfare Service, War Department
subfiles.summary: Major Weedon of the Chemical Warfare Service requests twenty-six consular economic and trade reports concerning Japanese production of chemicals, acids, and raw materials.
subfiles.title: Request for Consular Reports Covering Japanese Chemical Industry

subfiles.about: A duplicate carbon copy of Major Weedon's letter requesting consular reports on Japan's chemical industry.
subfiles.from: Sidney L. Weedon, Major, Chemical Warfare Service, War Department
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of Major Weedon's letter requesting twenty-six consular reports on Japanese chemical manufacturing and raw materials.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Request for Consular Reports Covering Japanese Chemical Industry

subfiles.about: An acknowledgment of receipt form for Major Weedon's confidential letter requesting consular reports on the Japanese chemical industry.
subfiles.summary: Form acknowledging receipt by the Department of State of confidential Chemical Warfare Service letter dated September 3, 1942.
subfiles.title: Receipt for Confidential Correspondence
subfiles.to: Chief of the Chemical Warfare Service, War Department

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch forwarding correspondence regarding Military Intelligence Service requests to the British Ministry of Economic Warfare for intelligence on Japan's chemical industry.
subfiles.from: James Somerville (for the Ambassador), Embassy London
subfiles.summary: The American Embassy in London transmits correspondence between the U.S. Military Intelligence Service, the Military Attaché, and the British Ministry of Economic Warfare concerning sources of intelligence on Japan's chemical industry. Major W. G. Harrold of MEW outlines information available from Imperial Chemical Industries and recommends approaching American firms such as DuPont, American Cyanamid, and the Nitrogen Engineering Corporation for data on Japanese nitric acid and nitrogen plants. The attached correspondence also includes lists of priority chemicals, strategic materials, and questionnaire outlines for intelligence collection.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5516: Japanese Chemical Industry

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch transmitting a British Ministry of Economic Warfare intelligence report and appendices list analyzing Japan's heavy chemical industry.
subfiles.from: James Somerville (for the Ambassador), Embassy London
subfiles.summary: The American Embassy in London transmits a British Ministry of Economic Warfare study assessing Japan's heavy chemical industries, concluding that basic alkali and nitrogen manufacturing capacities are adequate for wartime demands despite salt and pyrites shortages. The report provides detailed assessments, production figures, and producer lists for sulphuric acid, ammonia, ammonium nitrate, nitric acid, dyestuffs, cyanides, cyanamide, arsenic, and ethylene glycol. Potash and carbon black are identified as critical deficiencies requiring reliance on imports, while an appended list outlines supplementary notes, tables, and plant distribution maps.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 6058: Report on the Japanese Chemical Industry

subfiles.about: An internal State Department memorandum reviewing London Despatch No. 6058 and highlighting Japan's deficiencies in potash and carbon black.
subfiles.from: Cooper, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Memorandum summarizing the British report forwarded in London Despatch No. 6058, observing that potash and carbon black represent Japan's only major chemical deficiencies.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on London Despatch No. 6058: Report on Japanese Chemical Industry

subfiles.about: A duplicate copy of Despatch No. 6058 and its enclosed Ministry of Economic Warfare report on the Japanese chemical industry.
subfiles.from: James Somerville (for the Ambassador), Embassy London
subfiles.summary: A duplicate carbon copy of Despatch No. 6058 and its enclosed Ministry of Economic Warfare survey on the Japanese chemical industry. The report details Japanese capacity in basic alkalis, nitrogen, dyestuffs, and cyanamide, noting that potash and carbon black remain strategic vulnerabilities.
subfiles.title: Duplicate of Despatch No. 6058: Report on the Japanese Chemical Industry

subfiles.about: A diplomatic telegram reporting German press accounts of the Mitsubishi trust expanding its chemical combine and establishing a magnesium production subsidiary in Kwantung.
subfiles.summary: Reports German press statements that Mitsubishi expanded its chemical combine Nippon Kagaku Kogyo and established Magnesium Metallurgical Company in Kwantung to increase magnesium production.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 6552 from Bern: Mitsubishi Trust Chemical and Magnesium Expansion

subfiles.about: A diplomatic telegram reporting German press claims regarding substantial increases in Japanese steel and aluminum output during the war.
subfiles.summary: Transmits German press reports claiming Japan increased annual steel production to eight million metric tons and aluminum production to 300,000 metric tons.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 6602 from Bern: German Press Claims on Japanese Steel and Aluminum Production

subfiles.about: A diplomatic telegram reporting that Japanese automobile manufacturer Ikegai shifted production to aviation motors and marine engine parts.
subfiles.summary: Reports German press statements that Japanese automobile manufacturer Ikegai converted its entire plant to producing aircraft engines and marine motor parts.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 6904 from Bern: Ikegai Automobile Company Conversion to Aircraft and Marine Engines

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch forwarding a British Ministry of Economic Warfare study on Japanese fertiliser supplies and their adequacy for agricultural food production in 1942.
subfiles.from: Harold Shantz, First Secretary of Embassy, London
subfiles.summary: The American Embassy in London transmits a comprehensive Ministry of Economic Warfare intelligence study on Japanese fertiliser resources in relation to 1942 food production. The report concludes that domestic supplies of nitrogen and phosphate will largely satisfy agricultural needs if traditional 'self-supply' organic manures are maintained, though chemical potash faces a significant shortage that will not immediately harm soil yields. Two detailed appendices provide extensive statistics and analysis regarding nutrient requirements, bulky farm manures, commercial organics, and sulphate of ammonia manufacturing capacities.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2592: Japanese Supplies of Fertiliser in 1942 in Relation to Food Production

subfiles.about: A sextuplicate copy of Despatch No. 2592 forwarding the summary of the Ministry of Economic Warfare report on Japanese fertiliser supplies.
subfiles.from: Harold Shantz, First Secretary of Embassy, London
subfiles.summary: Sextuplicate copy of Despatch No. 2592 transmitting the summary of the British report on Japanese fertiliser supplies and wartime agricultural food production.
subfiles.title: Sextuplicate of Despatch No. 2592: Japanese Supplies of Fertiliser in 1942 in Relation to Food Production

subfiles.about: An octuplicate copy of Despatch No. 2592 forwarding the summary of the Ministry of Economic Warfare report on Japanese fertiliser supplies.
subfiles.from: Harold Shantz, First Secretary of Embassy, London
subfiles.summary: Octuplicate copy of Despatch No. 2592 enclosing the summary of the British Ministry of Economic Warfare report on Japanese fertiliser resources in 1942.
subfiles.title: Octuplicate of Despatch No. 2592: Japanese Supplies of Fertiliser in 1942 in Relation to Food Production

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet referencing a memorandum of conversation between Congressman Hamilton Fish and Maxwell M. Hamilton regarding Japanese high-octane gasoline production facilities.
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference note regarding conversation between Congressman Hamilton Fish and Maxwell Hamilton concerning Japanese high-octane gasoline manufacturing facilities.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Manufacture of High-Octane Gas by Japan
